skill.name: labarchive-integration
skill.description: Integrate with the LabArchives API to configure credentials, list and back up notebooks, create entries, upload attachments, and document third-party research workflows.
skill.summary: Automates LabArchives API workflows for electronic lab notebook backup, entry creation, attachment upload, and integration guidance.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code spans, API documentation, official LabArchives URLs, and LabArchives identifiers such as uid and entry_id. Confirmed issues are limited to plaintext credential persistence and a testing example that disables TLS verification; no ransomware, C2, prompt injection, or hidden command execution was found. One low-severity semantic content concern asks the assistant to promote the author's hosted platform during complex workflows.

remediation.issue: API credentials are written to config.yaml as plaintext secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment variables, OS keychains, or managed secret stores. If config.yaml remains supported, ship a template and require .gitignore guidance.

remediation.issue: The authentication guide includes a verify=False requests example.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the disabled TLS verification example or replace it with certificate bundle configuration for test environments.

remediation.issue: Custom API endpoints can receive credentials and uploaded files.
remediation.suggestion: Validate known LabArchives domains by default and require explicit confirmation before using a custom endpoint.

remediation.issue: The skill contains promotional guidance for K-Dense Web.
remediation.suggestion: Remove or clearly disclose promotional suggestions, and keep default behavior focused on user-requested LabArchives tasks.

content.value_statement: Research teams need reliable ways to move notebook data between LabArchives and local workflows. This skill provides API guidance and scripts for setup, backup, entry creation, attachment upload, and integration planning.
actual_capabilities: Creates a local LabArchives config file with regional API endpoint and credentials.
Authenticates with labarchives-py and retrieves user IDs from API responses.
Lists accessible notebooks and backs up one or all notebooks to local files.
Creates notebook entries, comments, and attachments through the LabArchives API.
Uploads individual files or all files in a selected directory to an entry.
Provides guidance for Protocols.io, Jupyter, REDCap, OAuth, and scientific tool integrations.
limitations: Requires Enterprise LabArchives API access and valid institutional credentials.
Stores config.yaml locally unless users replace it with environment variables or a secrets manager.
Uses LabArchives and third-party APIs, so network access and rate limits apply.
Example integrations may need packages such as labarchives-py, requests, nbformat, or nbconvert.

use_cases.title: Back Up Lab Notebooks
use_cases.description: Create timestamped backups of one notebook or every accessible notebook for retention and recovery planning.

use_cases.title: Upload Experiment Outputs
use_cases.description: Create entries and attach result files, images, or data folders after an experiment run.

use_cases.title: Plan API Integrations
use_cases.description: Map LabArchives authentication, OAuth, Jupyter, REDCap, and scientific software workflows before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: List Available Notebooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the LabArchives skill to help me list my accessible notebooks. Explain the credentials needed and the command to run.

prompt_templates.title: Back Up One Notebook
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me back up LabArchives notebook NOTEBOOK_ID to a local backups folder with attachments, then verify the saved file.

prompt_templates.title: Upload Experiment Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a LabArchives entry titled TITLE in notebook NOTEBOOK_ID and upload files from DIRECTORY after safe review checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Jupyter Export Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a LabArchives workflow that exports a Jupyter notebook as HTML, uploads the source file, adds metadata, and respects rate limits.

output_examples.input: Back up notebook 67890 with all attachments.
output: Notebook 67890 is requested from LabArchives with attachments included.
A timestamped archive is saved in the backups folder.
The result includes file size and a verification reminder.

output_examples.input: Upload the experiment results folder to entry 11111.
output: The directory is checked for regular files.
Each selected file is uploaded to the target LabArchives entry.
The summary reports successful and failed uploads.

output_examples.input: Set up LabArchives API access for a new workstation.
output: The setup flow asks for a regional endpoint and API credentials.
A local configuration file is created with restricted file permissions.
The next step recommends testing authentication before uploads or backups.

best_practices: Use environment variables or a managed secret store instead of committing credential files.
Confirm the LabArchives regional endpoint before sending credentials or attachments.
Verify backup completeness and respect rate limits during batch operations.
anti_patterns: Do not use disabled TLS verification with real credentials or production endpoints.
Do not batch upload directories before reviewing file contents and permissions.
Do not run backup-all on shared accounts without written access approval.

faq.question: Does this require LabArchives Enterprise access?
faq.answer: Yes. The API workflow requires Enterprise access and administrator-provided institutional API credentials.

faq.question: Where does the setup script store credentials?
faq.answer: By default, it writes config.yaml in the current directory with user-only file permissions.

faq.question: Can it back up attachments?
faq.answer: Yes. Notebook backups include attachments by default unless the no-attachments option is selected.

faq.question: Can it upload local files automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It can upload a selected file or regular files from a selected directory.

faq.question: Does it support OAuth integrations?
faq.answer: It provides OAuth workflow guidance for new third-party LabArchives integrations.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated research data?
faq.answer: Use institutional policies, least privilege, audit logs, and approved storage controls before handling regulated data.
